The error you're seeing is the usual async lazy-loading problem. It isn't specific to asyncpg; asyncpg is just the driver underneath `create_async_engine`.

**What causes it**
Accessing a relationship attribute that wasn't loaded by the original query triggers an implicit SQL query. In async code, SQLAlchemy can't run that query on the fly. One write-up puts it this way: the error appears when code reads a relationship like `user.posts` that the original query didn't load ([dev.to via scour.ing](https://scour.ing/@nmarshall/p/https://dev.to/ayush_kumar_085a0f2c54e3f/fixing-sqlalchemyexcmissinggreenlet-in-fastapi-and-async-sqlalchemy-20-4gha)). Another explains that the AsyncEngine can't load attributes after the fact, so everything needed must be loaded during the initial request ([matt.sh](https://matt.sh/sqlalchemy-the-async-ening)).

**Common fixes**
- **Eager-load per query.** Use `selectinload` or `joinedload` in the statement, for example `select(User).options(selectinload(User.posts))` ([dev.to via scour.ing](https://scour.ing/@nmarshall/p/https://dev.to/ayush_kumar_085a0f2c54e3f/fixing-sqlalchemyexcmissinggreenlet-in-fastapi-and-async-sqlalchemy-20-4gha)).
- **Make the default loading eager.** Set `lazy="selectin"` on the relationship so it always loads with the parent ([matt.sh](https://matt.sh/sqlalchemy-the-async-ening)).
- **Avoid triggering loads on expired objects.** After `commit()`, attributes expire, and reading them can raise this error too. One library's docs show this with a plain attribute read after commit ([PyPI async-sqlmodel](https://pypi.org/project/async-sqlmodel/0.1.3/)). Common remedies (from general SQLAlchemy practice, not this search) are `expire_on_commit=False` on the session, or calling `await session.refresh(obj)` before reading.
- **Catch accidental lazy loads during development.** Setting `lazy="raise"` on a relationship makes unintended loads fail with a clear message instead of this one.
- **Check for sync calls.** A related pitfall is calling sync ORM methods inside an async session ([fixdevs](https://fixdevs.com/blog/sqlalchemy-not-working/)).

**Caveats**
The search didn't surface an asyncpg-specific cause or fix, so the advice above applies to any async driver. If the error persists after eager loading, look for `await`-less access to relationships in serializers (for example, Pydantic models built from ORM objects after the session closes), since those are a frequent hidden trigger.

**MissingGreenlet (SQLAlchemy 2.0 docs, version 2.0.54)**

**Description:** The page doesn't give a detailed description of this error. It says the error occurs when a call to the async DBAPI runs outside the greenlet context that SQLAlchemy's AsyncIO proxy classes normally set up: "A call to the async DBAPI was initiated outside the greenlet spawn context".

**Cause:** The error usually happens when I/O is attempted somewhere that doesn't use `await`. With the ORM, it is nearly always caused by lazy loading. The page says lazy loading "is not directly supported under asyncio without additional steps and/or alternate loader patterns."

**Recommended fixes:** The page doesn't list fixes for this error. It refers to the section "Preventing Implicit IO when Using AsyncSession," which covers common ORM cases and ways to avoid lazy loads, including specific loader patterns.

**Documentation version:** The page is labeled "Release: 2.0.54 legacy version" with a release date of September 15, 2026.

[WebFetch note: this page's text is 116957 characters long and the answer above covers only characters 0 to 100000; the final 16957 were not read — to read on, call WebFetch again with the same url and offset: 100000.]

**Docs version:** SQLAlchemy 2.0.54 (the page is marked "legacy version").

**Lazy loading and expired attributes**
- "special care must be taken to avoid lazy loading or other expired-attribute access involving ORM relationships" (the page's ORM Synopsis section). Under asyncio, implicit I/O on attribute access must be avoided.

**`lazy="raise"`**
- "relationships can be declared with `lazy="raise"` so that by default they will not attempt to emit SQL." Explicit eager loading is then needed to load collections.

**Eager loading with `selectinload()`**
- "The most useful eager loading strategy is the `selectinload()` eager loader." The page uses it to load `A.bs` within the `await session.execute()` call. The excerpt does not discuss `joinedload()`.

**`expire_on_commit`**
- The page says expiration generally shouldn't be needed, because `Session.expire_on_commit` "should normally be set to `False` when using asyncio." This lets you read attributes after `commit()`.

**`AsyncSession.refresh()`**
- A lazy-loaded relationship "can be loaded explicitly under asyncio using `AsyncSession.refresh()`" when its name is passed in `attribute_names`. Eager loading is still preferred.

**`AsyncAttrs.awaitable_attrs`**
- Accessing an unloaded relationship can be done by awaiting it through the `awaitable_attrs` prefix, e.g. `await a1.awaitable_attrs.bs`. This requires the `AsyncAttrs` mixin, added in 2.0.13.

## SQLAlchemy MissingGreenlet with SQLAlchemy 2.x: research findings

**Decision:** Research only, so no ADOPT/EXTEND/COMPOSE/BUILD choice. The applicable fix is the documented async ORM loading pattern. Nothing has been reproduced or changed.

### Project context (local fixtures)
- `requirements.txt`: `SQLAlchemy==2.0.43`, `asyncpg==0.30.0`
- `project.md`: Python 3.12, async ORM session. MissingGreenlet fires when an unloaded relationship is read outside the awaited query. Root cause not reproduced.

### What the official docs say
Sources: [SQLAlchemy error XD2S](https://docs.sqlalchemy.org/en/20/errors.html#error-xd2s) (the `sqlalche.me/e/20/xd2s` short link redirects here) and [SQLAlchemy asyncio ORM docs](https://docs.sqlalchemy.org/en/20/orm/extensions/asyncio.html).

- **Cause:** The error means I/O ran outside the greenlet context that SQLAlchemy's async proxies set up. With the ORM it is nearly always a lazy load. Lazy loading is "not directly supported under asyncio without additional steps and/or alternate loader patterns."
- **Fixes the docs cover:**
  - Eager-load in the statement with `selectinload()`. This is the docs' most useful strategy.
  - Set `lazy="raise"` on relationships so accidental loads fail loudly during development.
  - Set `expire_on_commit=False` on the async session, which the docs say "should normally" be used with asyncio.
  - Load explicitly with `await session.refresh(obj, attribute_names=[...])`.
  - Use `await obj.awaitable_attrs.<rel>` with the `AsyncAttrs` mixin (added in 2.0.13).

### Community leads (snippets only, not read in full)
[dev.to write-up via scour.ing](https://scour.ing/@nmarshall/p/https://dev.to/ayush_kumar_085a0f2c54e3f/fixing-sqlalchemyexcmissinggreenlet-in-fastapi-and-async-sqlalchemy-20-4gha) and [matt.sh](https://matt.sh/sqlalchemy-the-async-ening) describe the same remedies (`selectinload`, `lazy="selectin"`). Treat them as corroboration, not authority.

Another common hidden trigger, from the search snippets: relationship access inside a serializer or Pydantic conversion after the session has closed. This is a lead I did not verify against the code.

### Applicability to this project
- The `asyncpg` driver is not the cause. The error is ORM-level, and `asyncpg` only sits underneath the engine.
- The `project.md` symptom matches the docs' cause exactly: an unloaded relationship is read outside the awaited query.
- Likely fixes, in order: add `selectinload` (or `lazy="selectin"`) on the query path that reads the relationship; set `expire_on_commit=False` if reads happen after commit; use `lazy="raise"` to find remaining implicit loads.

### Uncertainties
- **Version mismatch:** The docs I read are labeled 2.0.54. The project pins 2.0.43. The async guidance is stable across 2.0.x as far as I can tell, but I did not read the 2.0.43 docs, so this is unverified.
- **Truncation:** The docs pages were longer than what the fetch returned. I did not read the "Preventing Implicit IO when Using AsyncSession" section in full, which is the most relevant part.
- **Not reproduced:** No code, traceback or failing query was supplied, so I cannot say which relationship or path triggers the error.

### Next verification step
1. Pin the exact failing access path from the traceback, and confirm the relationship is read after the awaited query or after commit.
2. Set `lazy="raise"` on the suspect relationship and rerun the failing path. This surfaces every implicit load.
3. Add `selectinload` to that query, rerun, and confirm the error is gone. Check `expire_on_commit=False` if the read happens after commit.
4. Read the 2.0.43 "Preventing Implicit IO" section to confirm the same guidance applies to the pinned version.
